specGaps: SG-1 (503 envelope shape, APPROVED as drafted): §4.4 requires 'a 503 with a JSON error the fan-out engine understands' but no §2 schema pins the shape, and conductor never parses router 503 bodies itself (adapter/router-client.ts only health-probes; the real consumer is opencode's OpenAI-compatible provider client). RESOLUTION: the OpenAI-style envelope llama-server itself emits — HTTP 503, body {"error":{"message":<human reason>,"type":"unavailable_error","code":"queue_timeout"|"queue_overflow"}} — timeout vs overflow distinguished by `code`, which Task 11.7's metrics line can reuse.

SG-2 (the 'sane thread budget' for the clamp, APPROVED as drafted): RESOLUTION: a fixed 256-thread budget. When maxQueued + sum(maxInflightPerModel) + 8 > 256, effectiveMaxQueued = 256 - sum(maxInflightPerModel) - 8, logged at warn naming BOTH configured and effective values; if that arithmetic cannot reach effectiveMaxQueued >= 1, config validation FAILS naming admission.maxQueued (11.2's posture). The §2.2 defaults (64 + 4 + 8 = 76) are untouched.

SG-3 (no usable model field in the body, APPROVED as drafted): §4.4 says the router infers the model from the body's model field but not the failure case. RESOLUTION: bucket such requests under ONE reserved counter key (the empty-string model) with normal admission at interactive priority, and proxy them unchanged — never 400/reject (G5).

SG-4 (unrecognized X-Conductor-Priority value, APPROVED as drafted): RESOLUTION: treat exactly like untagged — interactive, admitted normally, no rejection. The §2.2 priorities config stays three keys; nothing is widened.

SG-5 (/conductor/health ownership straddles 11.4 and 11.7, APPROVED as drafted): 11.4's bullet requires the endpoint to ANSWER at a full queue, but the endpoint is listed under 11.7. RESOLUTION: 11.4 lands the MINIMAL route — GET /conductor/health -> 200 {"status":"ok"} — registered OUTSIDE admission (never admitted, never queued); 11.7 extends the body on the same route without changing the pool-exhaustion property. Note 11.3's pattern is /v1/.* only, so /conductor/* currently falls through to httplib's 404 — this route is genuinely new.
SG-6 (admission scope across /v1/*, APPROVED with the restatement above): admission applies to POST /v1/*; GET /v1/models bypasses it like /conductor/*.

assertions.text: with admission.maxInflightPerModel=2 and the stub upstream holding both in-flight requests open until released by the test, a third same-model POST /v1/chat/completions does NOT reach the upstream (stub hit count stays 2) and is QUEUED, not rejected; releasing one held request dispatches the queued one to the upstream and it completes with the upstream's response — proving both the at-cap block and the release/decrement wake-up, with NO sleeps (release-driven synchronization)

priority dequeue order interactive<review<batch (§2.2 priorities, lower value first): with the cap held, three requests tagged X-Conductor-Priority batch, review, interactive are enqueued in that deliberately INVERTED arrival order; releasing slots one at a time dispatches them interactive, then review, then batch; a request with NO header is treated as interactive yet still passes THROUGH admission (untagged bypasses nothing, §4.4), and the priority is read from 11.3's RequestTags rather than re-parsed

FIFO within a priority class: several queued requests of the SAME priority with distinguishable bodies are dispatched to the upstream in exactly their arrival order as slots free — observed at the stub, stable across the whole drain

a queued request waiting longer than admission.queueTimeoutMs receives HTTP 503 with the SG-1 envelope carrying code "queue_timeout", is removed from the queue, and NEVER reaches the upstream (zero stub hits for it); a subsequent release still wakes the remaining queued requests in the right order — the timed-out entry leaves NO HOLE

with the queue already holding exactly admission.maxQueued entries, the next request is rejected IMMEDIATELY (observably faster than queueTimeoutMs) with HTTP 503 and code "queue_overflow"; no already-queued entry is evicted and the upstream never sees the overflowed request

per-model independence: with model A at its in-flight cap AND holding a non-empty queue, a request whose body names model B is admitted straight through to the upstream with no queue wait (counters keyed on the body's model field); afterwards releasing A's held requests drains A's queue normally — B's traffic neither consumed nor blocked A's capacity

the POOL-EXHAUSTION test: with model A's in-flight slots all held open AND the queue filled to admission.maxQueued (every queued request occupying a blocked handler thread), GET /conductor/health still answers 200 promptly — the observable proof that the task queue is explicitly sized at startup via svr.new_task_queue with threads >= maxQueued + sum(maxInflightPerModel) + 8 instead of httplib's default pool, and that health is registered outside admission (SG-5)

config validation clamps maxQueued when maxQueued + sum(maxInflightPerModel) + 8 exceeds the 256-thread budget (SG-2): an over-budget config starts with the CLAMPED effective maxQueued — proven BEHAVIOURALLY by overflow 503s firing at the clamped bound, not the configured one — and logs the clamp at warn naming both values; the §2.2 default config is NOT clamped; a config whose clamp arithmetic cannot reach effective maxQueued >= 1 is REJECTED naming admission.maxQueued
